newsitem.title: FINLAND: INSTANT VIEW - Analysts on Finnish 1998 budget.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Analysts on Finnish 1998 budget.

text.p: Following are comments from Finnish analysts about the government's plans for the 1998 budget, after a senior finance ministry official said spending and the deficit would be below earlier plans:
"This is neutral or even a disappointment after there had been hopes for more drastic measures to balance the budget (after a report of such plans in daily Helsingin Sanomat last week)."
"Judging from (Finance Minister Sauli) Niinisto's comments earlier, there is leeway for a tax cut for the coming incomes settlement talks."
Says 1-2 billion markka worth of tax cuts could be an acceptable price for moderate pay hikes in 1998 to promote low inflation.
Sees long end bond yield stuck in a 15-25 basis point range above German 10-year Bund, unaffected by budget.
TEPPO KOIVISTO, TREASURY CHIEF ECONOMIST, OKOBANK:
"This is principally good news, especially that we got the deficit squeezed so tight, the target was not abandoned."
"The question is now that, if income taxes will be lowered after the pay deal by one to two billion markka, is that now included here?"
"This will hardly be seen in interest rates since Germany is so nervous at the moment."
MIKA ERKKILA, ECONOMIST, ENSKILDA HELSINKI BRANCH:
"Obviously (this strenghtens confidence in Finnish fiscal policy), as the deficit has not brought any negative surprises."
KIRSI HOKKA, CHIEF ECONOMIST, HANDELSBANKEN HELSINKI BRANCH:
"These figures look good compared with 191 billion and 21 billion". (referring to government plans in May for total spending and deficit).
"The main outlines seem quite good, but I want to see more details."
"Yes, it will strengthen confidence in Finnish fiscal policy."
